open_points.subject: installation operator
open_points.text: “agent token configured in the installation”; “service credentials and tokens live in the installation's protected configuration”; “the installation names” the listener address; “the host does not expose” it
open_points.question: Who is the actor trusted and authorized to create and change the installation configuration, token list, credentials, manifest locations, service instances, listener address and reverse-proxy exposure?
options: the owner operates the installation
a distinct platform operator operates it
an automated deployment identity operates it
open_points.default_guess: Treat a distinct trusted platform operator as responsible for installation configuration.

open_points.subject: owner channel and credential custody
open_points.text: “Reaches the kernel through the agent channel with the owner's token.”
open_points.question: What component is the owner's client on the agent channel, and can an agent or intermediary read, retain or replay the owner's token and thereby perform owner-only actions?
options: a trusted owner client sends the token directly through the proxy
the agent mediates the request but cannot access the token
the agent possesses and sends the owner token
open_points.default_guess: Use a trusted owner-controlled client that keeps the owner token inaccessible to agents.

open_points.subject: personal data received through direct service access
open_points.text: “the owner ... is the only reader of personal data”; “values of class `personal_data` reach an agent only as digest and class”; but the changed exclusion says an agent's direct service access is outside the kernel and “its personal-data promise (K-14) covers what the kernel itself returns,” while decision 17 says the agent processes a photo itself through such access
open_points.question: May an agent receive or read personal data directly from a microservice outside the kernel, or is the owner still the only reader across the whole system boundary?
options: agents may receive personal data directly; the restriction applies only to kernel responses
agents may access services but those services must enforce the same digest-only restriction
agents may never directly receive personal data
open_points.default_guess: Limit the digest-only promise to kernel responses and acknowledge that direct service access has a separate policy.

open_points.subject: secret echo detection
open_points.text: “A service's own answer body that echoes one verbatim is withheld from everyone ... and never used as an output.”
open_points.question: What exact byte or structural comparison constitutes a verbatim echo, which configured secrets are checked, and what observable run/node result is produced when a body is withheld?
options: withhold when the complete body equals a secret
withhold when any body byte range equals a secret
inspect defined response fields for exact secret values
open_points.default_guess: Check every response byte sequence against all credentials used for that request, fail the node with a non-secret reason, and store no body.

open_points.subject: outbound microservice connection
open_points.text: “Outbound, the kernel calls microservices over their HTTP APIs.”
open_points.question: How does the kernel authenticate a microservice endpoint and protect credentials, request data and responses in transit between the kernel and that service?
options: require HTTPS with verified service identity
trust a private network and permit plaintext HTTP
let each manifest operation declare its transport requirements
open_points.default_guess: Require HTTPS with normal certificate and hostname verification.

open_points.subject: surface authentication failures
open_points.text: “tokens are compared in constant time” and each action names its failure, but no action states the result of a missing, unknown, revoked or wrong-principal token
open_points.question: What observable refusal and audit record results when authentication fails or an authenticated actor attempts an action it is not authorized to perform?
options: one indistinguishable authentication/authorization refusal
distinct unauthenticated and forbidden refusals
transport-level rejection outside the action model
open_points.default_guess: Return one non-enumerating refusal to the caller while recording the internal reason without recording the token.

open_points.subject: meaning of the agent author right
open_points.text: The agent token “says whether the agent may author,” and agents “author functions and flows,” but “compose and prove a flow” is allowed to “agent” without the author-right qualification used for function authoring, trial cases, capture and rollback
open_points.question: Does the may-author flag gate flow composition and binding proposals as well as functions and trial-corpus changes?
options: gate every action that creates design records
gate only function and trial-corpus records
use separate rights for functions, flows and bindings
open_points.default_guess: Gate every action that creates or changes authored design records with the single may-author flag.

open_points.subject: agent inspection scope
open_points.text: “inspect functions, flows, runs, bindings, approvals, standing grants and effect attempts” is available to every agent, while K-12 says that for repair an agent receives only one slot and for composition receives contracts and bindings but not implementation bodies
open_points.question: How is an inspection request assigned to repair or composition context, and exactly which function implementations, traces and trial evidence may an agent inspect outside those contexts?
options: inspection requires an explicit repair or composition context
inspection always follows the stricter K-12 projection inferred from the requested object
agents may inspect everything except implementation bodies during composition
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit scoped context and enforce the corresponding K-12 projection.

open_points.subject: fixed MCP surface coverage
open_points.text: K-11 exposes “inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel,” but the primary actions separately require adding a trial case, capturing a failure, releasing a failed run, rolling back, proposing a binding, composing and proving a flow, and refusing an effect
open_points.question: Which fixed MCP operation carries each required primary action omitted from K-11, and is effect refusal a choice within `approve` or a separate operation?
options: expand the fixed operation set to name every action
define those actions as variants of `author`, `approve` or another listed operation
remove the unmatched primary actions
open_points.default_guess: Expose each materially different primary action as an explicit typed MCP operation, with approval and refusal as outcomes of one decision operation.

open_points.subject: agent activation over MCP
open_points.text: The primary action says “agent or owner asks” to activate a flow and permits an agent to request activation of a proven read-only version, while K-11 lists “the owner's ... activate”
open_points.question: Is `activate` callable by an agent for a proven read-only flow, or is it owner-only at the MCP authorization boundary?
options: agents may call it only for read-only versions
only the owner may call it
read-only activation occurs automatically during proof without an activation call
open_points.default_guess: Allow agents to call `activate`, with authorization determined by the proven effect classes.

open_points.subject: trial-case model
open_points.text: “add a trial case” produces “the case,” and cases have values that fit the contract's ports, but the text never defines what a case contains or what passing it asserts
open_points.question: Does a trial case contain inputs only, exact expected outputs, expected failure behavior, file fixtures, comparison rules or some combination, and what immutable identity makes two cases equal?
options: inputs plus exact expected outputs
inputs plus a requirement to succeed with schema-valid outputs
inputs plus explicit expected success, failure or output assertions
open_points.default_guess: Store canonical inputs and an explicit expected result consisting of success or a failure class, with optional exact expected outputs.

open_points.subject: capturing a failed execution
open_points.text: “capture a failed execution into the trial corpus” produces “the trial case every later implementation must pass,” although a failed execution may have no correct output
open_points.question: What assertion is derived from a failed execution, and who supplies any expected output needed to distinguish a repair from merely producing a different schema-valid result?
options: capture only the input and require future success
the actor supplies the expected output while capturing
capture the observed failure and require that exact failure not recur
open_points.default_guess: Capture the input and require a later execution to succeed and satisfy the contract, without asserting an exact output unless the actor supplies one.

open_points.subject: corpus changes versus current activation
open_points.text: Admission occurs “when an implementation is submitted,” while trial cases can be added later and “are not withdrawn”; rollback requires an implementation already admitted “over the current corpus” and “runs no admission”
open_points.question: When a case is added or captured, are existing implementations automatically re-evaluated, and what happens to a currently active implementation that fails the enlarged corpus?
options: re-evaluate all implementations and deactivate a failing current activation
re-evaluate only the current implementation and retain historical verdicts for others
leave existing activations and verdicts unchanged until implementations are resubmitted
open_points.default_guess: Re-evaluate the current activation immediately, deactivate it if it fails, and require explicit resubmission of historical implementations before rollback.

open_points.subject: contract-version currentness
open_points.text: “the first contract of a new slot name creates the slot”; rollback refers to “the slot's current contract version,” but no action says how a later contract version becomes current or what happens to the prior activation
open_points.question: What action or automatic rule advances a slot to a new contract version, and does that transition clear, preserve or coexist with activations of older contract versions?
options: authoring a new contract version makes it current immediately
the owner separately activates a contract version
each contract version remains independently addressable with no single current version
open_points.default_guess: Authoring a new contract version makes it current but leaves older immutable versions and their activations available only for historical runs.

open_points.subject: implementation submission, trial and admission sequence
open_points.text: There are separate actions to “author a function contract or implementation,” “try an implementation,” and automatically “admit and activate ... when an implementation is submitted”
open_points.question: Which request counts as submission, whether authoring automatically runs trials and admission, and what role the separate `try` action has before or after that automatic admission are not stated; what is the exact sequence?
options: authoring stores code and automatically performs trial, admission and activation
`try` submits the stored implementation and triggers admission
authoring first performs an ad hoc try, followed by a separate submit operation
open_points.default_guess: Authoring stores the immutable implementation; an explicit `try` runs evidence without activation, and a distinct submission request triggers whole-corpus admission and activation.

open_points.subject: flow boundary ports and run inputs
open_points.text: K-10 says “A flow's own inputs and outputs are values,” but K-07 defines only graph nodes, edges, maps and guards, and the `run a flow` action does not state the supplied input object
open_points.question: How are a flow version's boundary input and output ports declared, typed and classified, and what exact input does a caller provide when starting a run?
options: explicit typed boundary ports on every flow version
inputs and outputs inferred from unconnected node ports
a single generic value input and output
open_points.default_guess: Require explicit named boundary ports with schemas and disclosure classes and validate a named input object before creating the run.

open_points.subject: operation binding contents
open_points.text: “An operation binding gives one manifest operation typed input and output ports,” while approvals cover a fully built HTTP request and K-08 assigns authority to operation nodes
open_points.question: Where are the HTTP method, URL construction, headers, body encoding, response decoding, effect class, target, disclosure classes and idempotency-key placement declared, and which actor is trusted to define each of them?
options: all are authoritative fields of the manifest operation accepted through the binding
the agent supplies mappings and classifications in the proposed binding and the owner accepts them
the manifest supplies transport details while the proposed binding supplies typed mappings and classifications
open_points.default_guess: Make transport and effect metadata authoritative manifest fields, with the binding providing only owner-accepted typed mappings and the operation-record digest pin.

open_points.subject: effect-class definitions
open_points.text: “Effect classes are `read`, `draft-write`, `state-transition`, `external-effect`, `destructive`.”
open_points.question: What observable criteria distinguish these five classes, especially `draft-write` from `state-transition` and `external-effect` from `destructive`, so that operation authors and owners classify the same operation consistently?
options: normative class definitions based on externally observable consequences
service owners choose a class without kernel-enforced criteria
the kernel derives the class from HTTP method or operation metadata
open_points.default_guess: Define normative consequence-based criteria and have the service manifest declare the class for owner acceptance.

open_points.subject: service-call failure taxonomy
open_points.text: “their answers are untrusted data until validated at the port”; runs may be pending when “a service is unreachable” or when “an outcome [is] unknown,” but no boundary between these results is defined
open_points.question: For connection failure, timeout before or after bytes are sent, HTTP error, malformed response and output-schema failure, which node/run state results, and when is an effect considered definitely not sent, definitely applied or outcome unknown?
options: classify by a recorded request send/response boundary
treat every transport or response failure of an effect as outcome unknown
use service-specific failure declarations from the manifest
open_points.default_guess: Use an explicit send boundary: pre-send failures are unreachable, any ambiguous post-send effect failure is outcome unknown, and received invalid responses fail read nodes but leave effect nodes outcome unknown unless the service supplies conclusive evidence.

open_points.subject: approval output on unreachable service
open_points.text: The primary action promises that on approval “the effect runs on the exact input shown,” but settled question 14 explicitly allows “an approval whose effect was never sent” because the service was unreachable
open_points.question: What is the observable output of approving an effect when it cannot be sent: successful decision plus a pending run, an approval object, or a failed approval action?
options: the approval succeeds and the run becomes pending without a send
the approval action remains incomplete until a send occurs
the approval fails and must be repeated after resume
open_points.default_guess: Record a successful approval decision and return the attempt and run as pending; retain that approval for the unchanged request on resume.

open_points.subject: cancellation during an operation call
open_points.text: “cancel a run” promises “the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent” without stating what happens to an operation request already being transmitted or awaiting a response
open_points.question: At what execution points may cancellation take effect, and how are an in-flight effect and its possibly unknown outcome recorded?
options: cancel only between node executions
attempt transport cancellation and record an ambiguous effect as unknown
mark the run cancelled immediately while separately retaining the in-flight attempt's final status
open_points.default_guess: Stop scheduling new sends, let any in-flight call reach a recorded result, and require unknown-outcome resolution for an ambiguous effect before the run can become finally cancelled.

open_points.subject: run action result
open_points.text: “a run of the flow's active version, with outputs, or resting `awaiting_approval` / `pending`” omits the observable result when execution ends `failed`, `refused` or `cancelled`, and does not say whether the call waits for execution
open_points.question: Does `run a flow` return synchronously at the first rest or terminal state, return immediately with a run reference, or stream progress, and what typed result represents each terminal state?
options: execute synchronously until the first rest or terminal state
return immediately with a run reference and require inspection
stream trace events until rest or termination
open_points.default_guess: Execute synchronously until rest or termination and return a typed run snapshot covering every resting and terminal state.

open_points.subject: trace read failure
open_points.text: The table says “Each action names its observable output and its failure,” but `read a trace` has failure “—”
open_points.question: What happens when the trace or run reference is unknown, malformed, inaccessible to the actor or names data no longer available?
options: return an unknown-reference refusal
return an empty result
make trace reads collection queries that cannot reference a missing trace
open_points.default_guess: Return an unknown-reference refusal for a missing trace and an authorization refusal where applicable.

open_points.subject: value-schema system
open_points.text: “Every port carries a value schema. An edge is valid when both ports carry the same schema.”
open_points.question: What schema language and canonical equality rule define “the same schema,” including references, object-property order, numeric distinctions, optional fields and collection schemas?
options: JSON Schema with a defined canonical subset and canonicalization
a custom closed algebra of value types
byte-identical stored schema documents
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed, versioned schema algebra with structural canonical equality rather than unrestricted JSON Schema.

open_points.subject: map and guard execution semantics
open_points.text: “three structural forms: an edge, a map of a node over a collection, and a guard on a declared closed value”
open_points.question: What are the result ordering, failure propagation and trace identity for mapped executions, and what output/status is produced for a guard whose value does not select a branch?
options: ordered map with fail-per-element and skipped unmatched guards
ordered map with one failure failing the whole mapped node and skipped unmatched guards
parallel unordered map with aggregate results and an explicit required default guard branch
open_points.default_guess: Preserve input order, trace each mapped element, fail only dependent outputs for failed elements, and record unmatched guarded nodes as skipped.

open_points.subject: disclosure class origins and propagation
open_points.text: “Every value carries `open`, `business_confidential` or `personal_data`”; bindings classify service returns and functions output the highest class received, but no rule classifies caller-supplied flow inputs, constants or the output of a zero-input function
open_points.question: Who assigns those values' initial disclosure classes, what is the class ordering, and what class does a function receive when it has no classified inputs?
options: flow boundary declarations assign input classes and contracts declare a minimum output class
the caller supplies each input class and zero-input outputs are open
all non-service origins default to the most restrictive class
open_points.default_guess: Declare classes on flow boundary ports and function contracts, order them open < business_confidential < personal_data, and reject any value lacking a declared origin class.

open_points.subject: personal data in sandbox diagnostics
open_points.text: “An agent never receives a `personal_data` value,” while agent-written code is untrusted and trial evidence and traces expose failures, statuses and other diagnostics
open_points.question: How are stdout, stderr, exception messages, validation errors, resource diagnostics and trial evidence prevented from copying personal-data inputs into an agent-visible response or trace?
options: discard all free-form sandbox diagnostics
classify every diagnostic at the highest input class and redact it for agents
scan diagnostics for input values before returning them
open_points.default_guess: Discard unstructured stdout/stderr and classify every remaining execution diagnostic at the highest input class before surface disclosure.

open_points.subject: Python execution environment
open_points.text: “Functions are written in Python only” and use “the Python standard library only,” while admission must be deterministic
open_points.question: Which Python implementation, language version and standard-library version are part of an implementation's pinned execution environment, and what happens when that environment is upgraded?
options: one installation-wide pinned runtime version included in admission identity
runtime version stored per contract or implementation
always use the kernel's current Python runtime and re-admit after upgrades
open_points.default_guess: Pin one runtime image digest per implementation/admission and require re-admission under a new digest after upgrades.

open_points.subject: run pin set
open_points.text: “A run pins what it uses.”
open_points.question: Does a run pin only flow and function versions, or also bindings, manifest operation digests, selected service instances, schemas, sandbox runtime, disclosure metadata and request-building configuration?
options: pin every artifact needed to reproduce proof and execution
pin only flow and implementation identities
pin design artifacts but resolve service instance and credentials at send time
open_points.default_guess: Pin every immutable design and runtime artifact, while resolving credentials at send time and recording the concrete service instance/request used for each attempt.
